facts.statement: The species Faxinalipterus minimus was named and described in 2010 by José Fernando Bonaparte, Marina Bento Soares, and César Leandro Schultz.
facts.quote: The type species, Faxinalipterus minima was named and described in 2010 by José Fernando Bonaparte, Marina Bento Soares and César Leandro Schultz.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in 2002 and 2005 at a site 1.5 kilometers northeast of Faxinal do Soturno in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from the Caturrita Formation dating to 220–215 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fossils of the species were found in 2002 and 2005 at a site 1.5 kilometres northeast of Faxinal do Soturno, Rio Grande do Sul, from the Caturrita Formation dating from the Carnian-Norian, 220–215 million years old.

facts.statement: The hind limbs of Faxinalipterus are relatively long and better preserved than the front limbs.
facts.quote: The hind limbs, much better conserved than the front limbs, are relatively long.

facts.statement: An upper jaw fragment with three teeth was initially referred to Faxinalipterus but was later determined to belong to a distinct species named Maehary.
facts.quote: An upper jaw fragment, a left maxilla with three teeth, has been referred to the species, but later determined to represent an animal distinct from Faxinalipterus, which was named Maehary.

facts.statement: A 2022 study reinterpreted the fossils as belonging to the clade Lagerpetidae, a group of pterosauromorphs.
facts.quote: A study from 2022 reinterpreted the fossil remains and instead suggests them to belong to a member of the Lagerpetidae, another clade of pterosauromorphs.

facts.statement: Alexander Kellner suggested Faxinalipterus might be a basal pterosauromorph or a sister taxon to Ornithodira rather than a pterosaur.
facts.quote: However, Alexander Kellner has suggested Faxinalipterus might be not be a pterosaur but a basal member of the Pterosauromorpha instead or, if the lack of fusion between tibia and fibula is plesiomorphic, even a sister taxon of the Ornithodira.

facts.statement: Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia (2013) stated he could not find unequivocal pterosaur features in the fossils and noted the purported humerus is unlike those of Triassic pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia (2013) stated that he was "unable to find any unequivocal pterosaur features" in the known fossils of F. minima; in fact, according to the author, "the purported humerus is quite unlike the humeri of the Triassic pterosaurs".

facts.statement: Original describers considered Faxinalipterus perhaps the oldest known pterosaur, possibly predating European finds from the Norian.
facts.quote: They saw it as perhaps the oldest pterosaur known, as it possibly predates European finds from the Norian.

facts.statement: Because the Caturrita Formation consists of terrestrial sandstones, the original describers suggested Faxinalipterus evolved in a terrestrial habitat rather than a coastal one.
facts.quote: Because the Caturrita Formation consists of terrestrial sandstones, that evolution would have had its origins in a terrestrial, not coastal, habitat.

facts.statement: Original describers concluded Faxinalipterus was the most basal known pterosaur, citing features like a lack of tibia-fibula fusion, a thin radius, and an unfused coracoid.
facts.quote: They also concluded Faxinalipterus is the most basal known pterosaur, basal features including a lack of fusion between tibia and fibula, a thin radius and a coracoid that has not fused to the scapula.

facts.statement: Faxinalipterus lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype, UFRGS PV0927T, is held by the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul and consists of several partially fragmentary limb elements that may belong to a single individual.
rejected.quote: The holotype, UFRGS PV0927T, is part of the collection of the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul and consists of several, partially fragmentary, limb elements, perhaps of a single individual.

rejected.statement: Faxinalipterus was a small animal with an estimated humerus length of 18 millimeters, comparable in size to a sparrow.
rejected.quote: Faxinalipterus is a rather small animal, with an estimated total humerus length of eighteen millimetres. The size has been compared to that of a sparrow.

rejected.statement: A 2025 analysis suggests Faxinalipterus is a sister taxon to Ornithodira, more closely related to them than to Mambachiton and Aphanosauria.
rejected.quote: A 2025 analysis of Triassic avemetatarsalians by Garcia & Müller recovers the lagerpetids as a paraphyletic group to the pterosaurs, and Faxinalipterus not as a pterosauromorph but as a sister taxon to the Ornithodira, more closely related to them than to Mambachiton and Aphanosauria.
